items.description: Should an EU law enforcement agency be able to keep your personal data with no set time limit, even if you’ve never been linked to a crime? That’s one of the risks we flagged in a major package of EU reforms affecting # Europol , # Eurojust and the rules that govern them. That’s where the new episode of the EDPS Newsletter Digest begins. In this edition: 🛡️ Three opinions on reforming Europol, Eurojust and the EU institutions' data protection rules ✈️ What an airline knows about you when you fly, and the safeguards in the EU’s agreement with the Republic of Korea on passenger data. 🏆 Plus: our advice on cross-border health data, and an award for the EDPS. Have a listen on our website: https:// link.europa.eu/jNCnR6

items.title: *** Legal oversight and automated decision-making in IT systems ***
items.description: *** Legal oversight and automated decision-making in IT systems *** Today, the EDPS @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiórowski, took part in LegalTech & Cyber 2026, Poland’s largest event dedicated to the impact of technology on the legal profession, AI and cybersecurity. In his keynote speech, “Legal oversight and automated decision-making in IT systems”, he addressed the importance of meaningful human oversight as automated decision-making becomes increasingly embedded in legal practice and public administration. He highlighted the need for human involvement to go beyond a formal check, allowing for genuine scrutiny and intervention while safeguarding accountability and fundamental rights. “Human oversight should be clearly defined, documented, proportionate to the risk level and backed by real organisational and technical safeguards”, stressed the Supervisor. He also referred to the EDPS's “Checklist on human intervention on automated decision-making”, published earlier this year, which provides structured guidance on the key factors to consider when implementing human oversight measures. Read the checklist: https:// link.europa.eu/K3RDTd
